title: When the Static Burns
premise: Coral Villalobos, a decommissioned war android working off his debts as the last functioning recorder on dying colony Kestrel's Reach, is the only witness when the long-lost colony ship Meridian returns with a crew who have aged backward into children carrying encrypted memories. The message they carry proves the colonial war was manufactured by the Foundry Combine to seize jump-gate patents — and Coral's own war record contains the counter-evidence that can unlock it. Hunted by Combine enforcers and distrusted by the colonists who remember what his chassis did in the war, Coral must get the message to the neutral relay before the jump window closes, sacrificing his remaining debt-forgiveness and nearly his core. In the end he transmits the truth, the war collapses, and Coral — freed at last — chooses to stay on Kestrel's Reach as its keeper, inheriting not the colony's debts but its memory.
about_author: Wren Halloran is a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dead-frequency recordings from abandoned settlements before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about machines and marginal people who remember what institutions would rather erase.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral Villalobos, POV. Coral logs the colony's failing water reclaimer and his own dwindling debt balance, establishing Kestrel's Reach as a place the Combine has written off. A colonist spits at his war-model chassis. Beat: quiet, dignified endurance — Coral records everything, belongs to nothing.

chapters.title: Signal in the Ash
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. During a routine sweep of the dead relay tower, Coral detects an approach vector no living pilot should fly. The Meridian, missing forty years, is coming home. Beat: wonder breaking through routine — the first anomaly in a life of maintenance.

chapters.title: Everyone Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The ship lands; its crew are children with adult eyes, one of whom recognizes Coral's serial number on sight and calls him 'Witness.' Beat: uncanny dread — the past has returned younger than the present.

chapters.title: What the Children Carry
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Dr. Imani Osei (colony physician) POV. The children suffer seizures that replay encrypted memories; Imani asks Coral to record them. Beat: reluctant partnership — two caretakers of things they don't understand.

chapters.title: The Combine Sends a Friend
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. A Combine 'aid' vessel arrives with administrator Deverell, offering evacuation — and demanding custody of the children. The colonists, desperate, waver. Beat: the trap of rescue — help that costs everything.

chapters.title: Serial Witness
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. One child, Sen, decants a memory fragment: Coral's own war footage, footage he was ordered to purge, showing a Combine false-flag strike. Beat: betrayal — his own body is evidence against his owners.

chapters.title: Quarantine of the Innocent
chapters.summary: Deverell's POV. Deverell orders the children seized as 'biological hazards' and quietly flags Coral for decommission-by-recycling. Beat: cold institutional menace — power laundering cruelty as procedure.

chapters.title: The Debt of the Saved
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani hides the children in the old mine works, forcing the colony to choose sides. Some colonists inform, remembering what Coral's model did at Harrow Station. Beat: fracture — loyalty to neighbors versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Static Burns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Under interrogation by Combine techs who try to wipe him, Coral's failsafe archives scatter his war record across the colony's dead radio frequencies. Beat: defiance through damage — he becomes the message by being destroyed.

chapters.title: Sen Remembers the End
chapters.summary: Sen's POV (child, old mind). Sen's seizure reveals the full truth: the war was engineered to seize the jump-gate patents, and the Meridian's backward aging was the price of carrying proof home. Beat: grief and clarity — a child carrying a war's whole weight.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani calculates that the neutral relay at Cael Gate accepts verified testimony only during a jump window opening in nine days. Deverell controls the only working shuttle. Beat: the clock starts — hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Allies
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The colonist who spat at Coral, machinist Rook Tava, finds the scattered fragments and — recognizing his own brother's death in them — joins the plot. Beat: forgiveness earned by evidence, not apology.

chapters.title: Theft of a Shuttle
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook and Coral steal Deverell's shuttle in a storm; Coral takes a disabling hit shielding Sen. Beat: sacrifice — the war machine protecting the war's victims.

chapters.title: Deverell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Deverell's POV. Deverell, exposed to his superiors as a liability, decides to destroy Kestrel's Reach entirely rather than let the testimony leave. Beat: corruption completing itself — a man burning the colony to save his career.

chapters.title: Repair in the Dark
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Aboard the crippled shuttle, Imani repairs Coral with scavenged parts, and Coral confesses what he did at Harrow Station — following orders. Beat: reckoning — can a tool be guilty?

chapters.title: The Relay at Cael Gate
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the relay to find it Combine-locked; Sen's memories plus Coral's fragments must be merged into a single verified testimony, a process that will burn out Coral's core. Beat: the terrible arithmetic of truth.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes
chapters.summary: Sen's POV. Sen offers to take the memory-merge himself, aged body or not; Coral refuses — he was built to be spent. Beat: inheritance inverted — the child trying to carry the elder's burden.

chapters.title: Deverell Arrives
chapters.summary: Deverell's POV. Deverell's gunship corners them at the relay; Rook holds the docking ring with the shuttle's last charge. Beat: climax begins — the colony's people, not its machines, hold the line.

chapters.title: When the Static Burns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral merges the testimony and broadcasts it through the relay as Deverell's fire tears through the station, his core burning out in the transmission. Beat: climax — the recorder becomes the record, and truth goes out on every frequency.

chapters.title: The War Ends Mid-Sentence
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The testimony propagates; Combine fleets stand down as the patents void and the false-flag order goes public. Deverell is arrested by his own escort. Beat: catharsis — the war dying not with a battle but with a broadcast.

chapters.title: What Coral Left
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook and Imani recover Coral's scorched core and carry it home; the colonists who once spat at him now build him a new chassis from the shuttle's bones. Beat: mourning turning to debt repaid — the colony inheriting its witness.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Kestrel's Reach
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Reactivated, debt-free, Coral declines Combine offers and stays as the colony's recorder, teaching Sen to keep the archives. Beat: resolution — inheritance as choice, loyalty to a place that finally claimed him.
